title: Common definitions
description: The envelope and the shared types every Atrio artifact builds on (ADR-014). Identifiers are English because the artifact contract is code, not prose; the project language (artifactLanguage) governs the content a team writes, and translation of labels belongs to presentation.

schemaVersion.description: Schema generation of this artifact, monotonic per artifact type. Version N reads N-1 and N-2 and always writes N; N-3 and older migrate through an intermediate release.

ulid.description: ULID in canonical form: 26 characters of Crockford base32, uppercase. The alphabet excludes I, L, O and U, and the first character is bounded by the largest representable timestamp.

timestamp.description: An instant in RFC 3339 form, with offset.

actor.description: Who produced a change: a human, identified by the git identity of the project, or an agent, identified by the display name the project declared for it.

name.description: git user.name for a human; the declared displayName for an agent.

email.description: git user.email. Required for a human: the platform blocks until git identity is complete, so an attributed change always carries both halves of it.

agentId.description: Canonical definition the agent was materialized from.

human.description: An actor narrowed to a person. Deployment and test confirmations are never attributable to an agent.

catalogId.description: The identifier half of a catalogRef: an agent, a skill, a pack or a flow as the official catalog names it. It stands alone in the marketplace manifest, where the version is the manifest's own platformVersion and repeating it per item would invite the two to disagree. A test keeps this pattern and catalogRef's from drifting apart.

catalogRef.description: A definition from the global cache, as id@version: an agent, a pack or a flow. Every place that names one — a declaration, a flow being executed, an agent an event is about — says it the same way, because they all point at the same catalog.

capability.description: One entry of the closed capability catalog the platform governs (ADR-013): what an item needs from a provider to be installable, and what feeds the countermeasures when a provider lacks it. Membership in the catalog is checked by the core, not here. The catalog is closed by T-050, which runs after the manifest is public, and the spec that names eight entries closes them with an ellipsis — pinning them into this contract would make the ninth capability a breaking change to a published API rather than a platform release.

roleId.description: A canonical role an agent plays: architect, product-owner, idea-explorer. A role is not an agent — two definitions can play the same one, and a flow names the roles that take part in a stage while the project binds each role to the agent it declared for it. Four documents spell it: the manifest, an agent's definition, a flow's definition and a flow's progress.

stageId.description: A stage's identifier within the flow that declares it. The definition names it and the progress artifact records what happened to it, so both say it the same way.

artifactType.description: The kinds of artifact a reference can point at and a flow stage can produce. The catalog is closed: widening it is a schema change.

languageCode.description: A language as an ISO 639-1 code.

localizedText.description: Text shown to a person, keyed by ISO 639-1 code. Spanish and English are both mandatory (ADR-014); the map stays open so a third language is data rather than a change to the contract. It lives here because the marketplace, an agent's definition and a flow's stages all show text to the same person. The keys are constrained with patternProperties and not with propertyNames: a propertyNames failure carries no instance location at all, so the rejection could not name the field it came from.

providerScope.description: Which providers something can be installed on: every one, or a closed list. A feature exclusive to one provider is announced to the user and installable only there (01-definicion-producto.md, section 4.2). A definition declares its own scope and the marketplace manifest indexes it, so the catalog and the definition can never be two opinions.

definitionPath.description: A path inside a definition of the catalog, relative to that definition's own root. Forward slashes only, and no segment can be . or .. — the pattern makes escaping the provider folder on materialization unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged. It lives here in a single copy on purpose: a second copy of a security rule is a copy that can rot.

providerId.description: An agent CLI provider, as the platform names it: claude-code and, from M2 on, the others. The same spelling identifies a provider wherever it appears — the project's provider list, the per-provider settings of an agent, and the providers an item of the marketplace can be installed on.

platformVersion.description: An Atrio release, as the tag that ships it.

permissionCategory.description: The seven categories the core arbitrates (01-definicion-producto.md, section 9). Closed catalog: widening it is a schema change, not a free edit. agents.json declares a level for each one; an authorization event in the log names the one it is about, and a test keeps both lists from drifting apart.

branch.description: A working branch: one task, one branch. The length of the short ULID prefix is fixed by the branch creation rules, not here.

reference.description: A typed pointer to another artifact.

documentEnvelope.description: The reduced envelope of a document's front-matter. It carries identity and schema generation and nothing else: a markdown file is hand-edited, and timestamps or attribution copied there by hand would rot against git, which already knows both (ADR-014, attribution by git identity).

definitionEnvelope.description: Carried by every canonical definition of the catalog: an agent, a flow. Like the manifest, a definition is not an artifact of a project — it is published by the definitions repository, so it has no ULID and no git identity to attribute it to — and unlike the manifest it carries no version of its own: definitions are versioned by the tag that ships them, and the manifest of that tag is what joins this id to a version.

manifestEnvelope.description: Carried by the marketplace manifest, and by nothing else. The manifest is not an artifact of a project: the official definitions repository publishes it per tag, so it has no ULID of its own and no git identity to attribute it to, and giving it the artifact envelope would mean inventing both. manifestVersion is the schema generation under the name the public API uses (ADR-005: the manifest follows the same standard as the artifacts).

envelope.description: Carried by every JSON artifact. Composed with allOf, so artifacts close themselves with unevaluatedProperties rather than additionalProperties.
